fix_commit.message: Strengthen the fts5_locale() function against integer overflow attacks, even when SQLite is compiled with oversize values for SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Integer overflow in fts5LocaleFunc() blob size computation
findings.message: fts5LocaleFunc() (the implementation of the SQL function fts5_locale(LOCALE, TEXT)) declares nLocale, nText and nBlob as plain 'int' and computes nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText before allocating the result buffer with sqlite3_malloc(nBlob). sqlite3_value_bytes() returns an int whose value can approach SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH; when SQLite is built with an oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH (a supported, documented compile-time option), the sum nLocale + 1 + nText can exceed INT_MAX and wrap around to a small or negative 'int' value. That truncated/wrapped value is then passed to sqlite3_malloc(), which allocates a buffer far smaller than the amount of data (nLocale and nText bytes) subsequently memcpy'd into it via memcpy(pBlob, zLocale, nLocale) and memcpy(&pBlob[nLocale+1], zText, nText), resulting in a heap buffer overflow. The bug requires a non-default build configuration (oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH) to be reachable, since with the default SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH (1,000,000,000) the sum cannot overflow a 32-bit int.
findings.suggestion: Declare nLocale, nText and nBlob (and the analogous nBlob variable in the later refactored version of this function) as 64-bit (sqlite3_int64 / i64) instead of int, so that the addition nLocale + 1 + nText cannot wrap around a 32-bit boundary, and allocate with sqlite3_malloc64() (which accepts a 64-bit size) instead of sqlite3_malloc(). This matches the upstream fix, which widened the types and switched to sqlite3_malloc64().

ground_truth.root_cause: Lengths obtained from sqlite3_value_bytes() (an int, bounded in principle only by the compile-time SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH) are stored and summed using 32-bit 'int' arithmetic (nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText) and then passed to the 32-bit-size-parameter sqlite3_malloc(), instead of using a 64-bit type and sqlite3_malloc64() throughout the computation and allocation.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Integer overflow in fts5LocaleFunc() blob size computation
